Carvallo Lerena', 8 July 1896. Machine transcript only, nothing tiered. See corrections, 12 October.

src: FamilySearch record index - the department of ARTIGAS, Uruguay, surveyed on eight spellings of the surname
what: A department this archive had never opened, found via a cross-spelling sweep
note: COUNTS WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY. q.anyPlace FALLS BACK TO THE COUNTRY: 'Nonesuch, Uruguay' - a department that does not exist - returns 1,787, the whole-country figure, and records indexed only to 'Uruguay' satisfy every departmental query. Of the first hundred Artigas hits, 15 name Artigas, 28 name somewhere else, 57 carry no place at all. The Osaka control proved the filter binds on COUNTRY, not on DEPARTMENT. WHAT SURVIVES: the nulls (Juan Carlos as subject 0, as father 0, Lerena x Lerena 0) are if anything strengthened, because an over-wide filter cannot hide a record; and Benito Lerena's Artigas household is real - five infant deaths registered at Artigas 1893-1902, and Teodoro Alves Lerena's birth registered at Artigas in 1907, all explicitly placed there. WITHDRAWN: that Domingo and Asuncion Lerena are of Artigas, and that the 1896 death of Pedro a Lerena is an Artigas death - it is Montevideo. See corrections, 12 October.

src: FamilySearch record index - Uruguay Civil Registration: the 1896 death of 'Pedro a Lerena', certificate 353

note: Died 6 November 1896 aged 69, registered the next day; father Pedro A. Lerena, mother VICENTA DE LA VEGA, spouse MANUELA LEMOS. Volunteer-indexed, not machine-indexed. THE VOLUME IS 'Montevideo. Death Records 1896' - NOT Artigas, where a departmental place filter had placed it; that error is corrected the same day. Montevideo is the city the c.1833 census puts Pedro LERENA Vega in, so the fit improves. NOT MERGED: the two birth years disagree by a decade and both are age-derived. The act has not been opened.

src: FamilySearch record index - Avelino Lerena worked across Uruguay (34 records), and the Cordon's first four leads
what: Whether the Cordon can attach the Traibel branch to Sancho
note: THREE OF THE FOUR LEADS TURNED INTO CORRECTIONS OF THIS ARCHIVE. (1) Avelino is already attached - two baptisms of his children at San Francisco de Asis, 12 March 1858, name his parents; he is Avelino LERENA Fernandez, son of Sancho, d. Montevideo 23 Aug 1890. The note in compound-surname-sweep.tsv saying no record names his parents had been stale for a month and is corrected in place. (2) The 'second wife' Celedonia VILLADEMOROS belongs to his son Avelino Eduardo, already held with four children. (3) GENUINELY NEW AND UNEXPLAINED: an Avelino Lerena buried at the Cementerio Central de Montevideo on 2 June 1860 (Find a Grave Index, ark 1:1:QVKR-45SK) - a third man of the name, answering to nobody in this register. Derivative index, not an act; the burial register has not been opened. (4) The Paraguayan Manuel Antonio Lerena and the Carvallo Lerena household are untouched. 469 of the Cordon's 470 pages remain unturned and the errand stays open.

src: FamilySearch record index - Manuel Antonio Lerena traced out of a Cordon snippet, and the Pedro A. Lerena x Manuela Lemos household
what: The last of the four Cordon leads - a Manuel Antonio Lerena recorded 'paraguayo'
note: He is born at MONTEVIDEO on 31 March 1883, christened 9 April, son of Pedro A. Lerena and Manuela Lemos; later married Esther EVIA with sons Manuel Walter (b. 16 Nov 1921) and Alberto Nestor. So 'paraguayo' is either a different man or the machine's reading - the same transcript writes Montevideo as 'Monterdes', and the whole index holds ONE Lerena record in Paraguay. THE REAL YIELD IS A CONVERGENCE: the 1896 death of Pedro a Lerena gives his spouse as MANUELA LEMOS and his parents as Pedro A. Lerena and VICENTA DE LA VEGA - which is the parentage of Pedro LERENA Vega, counted at 16 in Montevideo household 229 c.1833. The Manuela Lemos row, entered 11 October, says in terms that which Pedro she married was not settled. Index-level both sides; the death act is now raised as an errand.

src: FamilySearch - Montevideo, Death Records 1896: acta No. 353 of 7 November 1896, read at the plate
what: Whether the Pedro who married Manuela Lemos is the son of Pedro Antonio Lerena and Vicenta Vega
note: SETTLED. No waypoint established - image ark and apid TH-909-72188-82458-0 only. PEDRO LERENA, nacido en Montevideo, 69, casado, died 6 November 1896 at calle Rivera 163 of tisis pulmonar (Dr Vitale), before Vicente Carricaonde, Juez de Paz of the 15th section. 'Hijo legitimo de Don PEDRO A. LERENA, oriental, fallecido, y de Dona VICENTA DE LA VEGA, oriental, fallecida.' Wife Dona Manuela, oriental, 53. Children named: ANTONIO, CARLOS TEODORO, MANUEL ANTONIO, plus the first declarant Don Pedro A. Lerena, soltero, empleado, 'hijo del fallecido'; second declarant Angel V. Garcia, 25. ALSO BREAKS A DATE: 69 in 1896 means born c.1827, so he is six in the census this archive dates c.1833, not sixteen - re-dating household 229 is now its own errand.

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay census, Montevideo household 229, read at the plate
what: The date of the enumeration three birth years in this register are derived from
note: CONTESTED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. No waypoint established - image ark and apid TH-1951-36718-25784-7 only. The household reads: 229 - D. Pedro A. Lerena, varon, 40 | D.a Vicenta Vega, muger, 35 | D.a Emilia Lerena, 18 | D.n Pedro D.o, varon, 16 | D.a Vicenta D.o, muger, age struck. FamilySearch labels the volume 'Montevideo. Census 1850'; this archive dates the household c.1833, inferred from the head at forty matching Pedro Antonio Lerena b. 31 July 1793 - a couple attested independently in 1837 and 1852. A man born 1793 is 40 in 1833 and 57 in 1850. A third anchor, the son's 1896 death act (sixty-nine), wants a census of about 1843. No two agree. The attachment is unaffected - the death act names his parents - but the birth years of Emilia, Pedro and Vicenta LERENA Vega are now marked as resting on an unestablished date.

src: FamilySearch catalogue koha:1408224, 'Uruguay, Montevideo, censos, 1726-1860' - film 7499042 read item by item
what: The date of the enumeration behind Montevideo household 229
note: SETTLED. The catalogue lists the film's items: item 1 = Padrones de habitantes, LIBRO 263, 1843; ITEM 2 = LIBRO 264, 1850; item 3 = libro 257, 1852-1853; libro 267, 1858. Household 229 is in item 2, so the enumeration is the padron of 1850 and this archive's c.1833 is withdrawn. Three derived birth years moved seventeen years later, and the head - entered at forty, so born about 1810 - is not Pedro Antonio Lerena born 31 July 1793; that holds under the 1843 book too, where he would be born about 1803. METHOD NOTE: the old date was inferred from the identification it was then used to support, and a catalogue entry naming the actual register book is what broke the circle - a volume label would not have.

src: FamilySearch catalogue koha:1408224 - film 7499042 read item by item, all six items
what: Whether a census 'of about 1833' was ever available on the film household 229 sits on
note: ALL SIX ITEMS READ. item 1 = libro 263, 1843 | item 2 = LIBRO 264, 1850 | item 3 = libro 257, 1852-1853 | item 4 = libros 265 and 258, 1852-1853 | item 5 = libro 267, 1858 | item 6 = libro 268, 1860. src: FamilySearch - Montevideo padron of 1850 (libro 264), casa 229 of CALLE SARANDI, read at the plate
what: Where Leonarda Margarita Lerena Vega was in 1850, absent from her parents' house
note: ANSWERED, AND MORE. No waypoint established - image ark and apid TH-1961-36718-27970-97 only. Leonarda is entered at casa 229 of CALLE SARANDI, blanca, oriental, aged 11 (she was 13). Her parents are at a DIFFERENT casa 229 on another street - two houses of the same number in one padron, so 'household 229' was never an identifier. SHE IS THE ONLY WHITE PERSON IN THAT HOUSE: Estanislada 20 (morena), Sinforiano 19, MANUELA 60 with patria AFRICA and casada, and Rosa 46 (oriental, casada) all carry the surname by ditto. Four people entered in the register in their own right. The census has no column for condition; that the surname reached them as Barbara's reached her son (1846, 'esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena') is filed as an INFERENCE. A Cordon or Catedral burial would say the word outright - raised as an errand.

src: FamilySearch full text - 'esclava de Alejandro Lerena' as a phrase, and the San Jose de Mayo baptism register 1841-1869 read at the transcript
what: Whether any parish act names an enslaved person in a Lerena household beyond the one already held
note: TWO DOCUMENTS, both San Jose de Mayo: the burial of 28 April 1846 (already held) and THE BAPTISM OF 25 APRIL 1846, which this archive did not have. The baptism: 'bautice solemnemente a Car[melo] Anselmo, que nacio el VEINTIUNO del mismo, hijo natural de BARBARA LERENA, NATURAL DE ESTA VILLA, ESCLAVA DE DON ALEJANDRO LERENA: fueron Padrinos Jose Carreras y Petronila Escobar.' Two nulls built on that shape were about to be recorded and were caught by running the known phrase as a control.

note: NOT FOUND YET, AND THE NULLS ARE WEAK. The record index holds nothing for Estanislada or Sinforiano under Lerena or Serena. Full text as compound phrases returns nothing - but the compound is the wrong shape, since such people are commonly entered by forename alone, exactly as Barbara is on the 1846 burial. The forename alone is too common to sweep: 'Sinforiano' with a Cordon place filter returns four pages. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, and it is encouraging: the vocabulary IS searchable - 'esclava' with a Cordon place filter returns 49 pages, concentrated in the baptism registers of 1818-1841 and the death register of 1809-1828. The errand to read the Cordon burials 1839-1852 for these four stands.

src: FamilySearch full text - the parish formula 'esclava/esclavo/liberta de [holder]' swept against every Lerena holder this archive can name
what: Whether any transcribed parish act names a Lerena as holder of the four who carry the surname at Sarandi 229 in 1850
note: CONTROLLED NULL, WITH TWO CONTROLS PASSING. Positives: 'esclava de Don Sancho Lerena' returns the Montevideo Catedral baptism register 1811-1813 (the act of 26 Sep 1812, Maria Mercedes daughter of Juana); 'esclava de Don Alejandro Lerena' returns the San Jose de Mayo baptism 1841-1869 and death 1839-1851 registers (Barbara and Carmelo Anselmo, April 1846). Nulls: 'esclava de Don Pedro Antonio Lerena', 'esclava de Pedro Lerena', 'esclava de Luis Lerena', 'esclavo de Don Sancho Lerena', 'liberta de Don Pedro Lerena'. SO THE ONLY TWO LERENA HOUSEHOLDS WITH A SURVIVING TRANSCRIBED ACT NAMING THEM AS HOLDERS ARE THE TWO ALREADY IN THIS REGISTER. The four at Sarandi 229 are not reachable this way - their acts may use 'parda libre' or name no holder, which is how Barbara appears on the burial. METHOD: the abbreviation D.n matches NOTHING; 'Don' matches; dropping the honorific matches.

src: South African Government Gazette via Gazettes.Africa - the surname across all 54,441 South African gazettes, 1910-2026, all five result pages walked
what: Open question 2 - whether Pablo Armando Lerena was ever gazetted as a consul of any rank
note: CONTROLLED NULL ON ONE SPELLING. Controls: coverage 1910-2026, 54,441 SA gazettes; 'exequatur' returns 644 documents with pre-1950 hits in 1914, 1932, 1933 and 1937, so the period and the consular vocabulary are both searchable. RESULT: the surname appears in 35 South African documents and the EARLIEST IS 1951 (Gazette 4584, the estate notice already held). Nothing across his Cape Town life, c.1908-1950. The gazette's formula is 'Recognition granted as Consul-General' / 'Vice-Consul', and honorary consuls ARE gazetted ('Withdrawal of the Recognition as Honorary Consul of Finland'), so the honorary reading does not explain the absence. CAVEATS: the site's country= parameter DOES NOT BIND - Mozambique documents appear in a country=za search - so the SA subset was taken by filtering result links on the /akn/za prefix; and the SPELLING VARIANTS HAVE NOT BEEN SWEPT.

what: Whether a Lavina dispensation is the marriage of Xavier Lavina to Leonarda Lerena
note: IT IS NOT, and that is the useful part. IT ALSO TESTED THE PREVIOUS DAY'S CONCLUSION: the 12 October sweep found no tenth Lerena dispensation using eight compound LERENA forms; this document would have been invisible to that sweep because it is filed under LAVINA, and it turns out not to be a counter-example. The conclusion survives a test it was not designed for - and the next doubt is now named: a Lerena BRIDE whose dispensation is filed under her husband's surname.

src: UK National Archives Discovery - AIR 54/52, 53, 54 and 185 (South Africa Air Force operations record books, 1942-1944), downloaded and machine-read for the surname LERENA and the other archives' surnames
what: David's free order 3689478 (four digitised pieces, 2,892 images: AIR 54/52 707, 54/53 708, 54/54 705, 54/185 772, each checked against TNA's listed image ranges) was run through macOS text recognition and searched with fuzzy matching (edit distance 2 for LERENA, LLERENA, LERINA). NO LERENA IN ANY FORM: the only near-misses were checked on the page images and are 'A/Sgt Levin' (twelve pages), 'Mc Laren' and similar. The pieces hold several units' books, not only 12 Squadron's. The scans are typed and the recognition read common names correctly (Levin was recovered on twelve pages) but it is NOT a line-by-line reading, and crew lists, not full nominal rolls, are what most pages hold, so this does not show he was not in 12 Squadron: ground crew are seldom named. Not walked. The other archives' surnames (Booyzen, Defranceski/Franceschi, Falco, Mazza, D'Arcy, Luwinski, Blazevic) and the Pablo-circle names Knott, Kannemeyer, Theys, Higgens and Chappell: nothing but noise (e.g. 'San Francesco', 'Bailey').
